Pane primitives

Agent primitive

An agent pane runs an agent CLI such as Claude Code or Codex. The agent primitive lets a plugin find the agent in a pane, read its activity and session, read the last prompt the user submitted, add toolbar buttons, send actions that the agent understands, and register signatures for agents the host does not know.

The kernel owns the process walk, the screen snapshot and every key write. The plugin owns the signature (how to recognise the agent) and the classifier (what the agent is doing now).

What you need

Grant Needed for
agent.read agents, view, session; the events agent-identified, agent-activity-changed and agent-goal-changed
agent.signatures The signatures manifest entry, the detector export and register-signature
agent.control set-toolbar-state and the intent agent-action
agent.read-prompts The event input-submitted and last-prompt. High risk: it exposes what the user typed.
fs.read:agent-sessions:<agent> Reading the transcript file that session points to

agent-action needs only agent.control. The kernel checks the activity itself, so the plugin does not need agent.read to send an action.

The detector and runtime signatures run on the server side. Toolbar state and agent actions also work from the client side. Plugins are written in Rust (stable 1.90 or later with the wasm32-wasip2 target) or TypeScript (Bun 1.2 or later). See toolchain setup.

Interface

// ilium:types/tree
enum agent-activity { none, working, idle, awaiting-approval, done, menu }
record agent-view {
    signature: string, activity: agent-activity, objective: option<string>, goal: option<string>,
}

// ilium:primitives/agent
record agent-pane { pane: node-id, view: agent-view }
record session-ref { scope: string, path: string, session-id: string }
record signature-action { id: string, keys: string, allowed-when: option<list<agent-activity>> }
record signature-spec {
    id: string, process-names: list<string>, aliases: list<string>, icon: option<string>,
    resume: option<list<string>>, actions: list<signature-action>,
    session-scope: option<string>, submit-keys: option<string>,
}
agents: func() -> list<agent-pane>;
view: func(pane: node-id) -> option<agent-view>;
session: func(pane: node-id) -> option<session-ref>;
last-prompt: func(pane: node-id) -> option<string>;
register-signature: func(spec: signature-spec) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
set-toolbar-state: func(button: string, pane: option<node-id>, enabled: bool,
    label: option<string>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;

The detector export is a separate contract, so a plugin can implement it without registering signatures at run time:

// Excerpt of ilium:exports/detector in reference-wit
// ilium:server/detector
record detector-process { name: string, argv: list<string> }
record detector-screen {
    columns: u16, rows: list<string>, cursor-row: u16, title: option<string>, revision: u64,
}
record classification { activity: agent-activity, objective: option<string>, goal: option<string> }
identify: func(processes: list<detector-process>) -> option<string>;
classify: func(signature: string, screen: detector-screen) -> classification;

Functions

Function (Rust / TypeScript) Grant Returns Meaning
agents() / agents() agent.read list<agent-pane> One entry per identified agent pane. Empty when the grant is declined.
view(pane) / view(pane) agent.read option<agent-view> Signature and activity of one pane. None when the pane is not identified or the grant is declined.
session(pane) / session(pane) agent.read option<session-ref> Transcript reference. Only a signature with session_scope yields one.
last_prompt(pane) / lastPrompt(pane) agent.read-prompts option<string> Last prompt submitted to the pane. None when the grant is declined.
register_signature(spec) / registerSignature(spec) agent.signatures result<_, plugin-error> Adds a signature, or replaces one the same plugin added at run time.
set_toolbar_state(...) / setToolbarState(...) agent.control result<_, plugin-error> Enables or relabels a toolbar button.

All of them are synchronous and take no request id. The Rust module is ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent; the TypeScript import is @ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent. Types follow the SDK naming rules: AgentPane, SessionRef, SignatureSpec and SignatureAction in Rust, with the same fields in camelCase in TypeScript. AgentActivity and AgentView come from ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree.

set_toolbar_state with pane: None sets the state for every agent pane that shows the button. With a pane id it sets that pane only, overrides the all-pane state, and is dropped when the pane closes. A label of None keeps the current label. A label over 32 cells is invalid-argument.

Activity values are none (not identified yet), working, idle, awaiting-approval, done and menu. In Rust they are AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval and so on; in TypeScript they are the strings 'awaiting-approval' and so on.

Signatures

A signature describes one agent program. Plugin signatures from the manifest and from register-signature share one set of rules:

Manifest key Field Default Rule
id id required 1 to 64 characters from [a-z0-9-]. The global id is <plugin-id>.<id>.
process_names process-names required 1 to 32 names, each non-empty, at most 255 bytes, with no / unless absolute.
aliases aliases none At most 32 entries.
icon icon none A Tabler icon name.
resume resume none An argv template. {session} is replaced by the session id.
actions actions none At most 32 actions. Each keys value is at most 1 KiB.
session_scope session-scope none A scope such as agent-sessions:claude.
submit_keys submit-keys "\r" Keys that submit a prompt in this agent.

Each action may set allowed_when, a list of activities in which the action is allowed. The default is ["idle", "done", "awaiting-approval", "menu"], so a compact action is refused while the agent works. Built-in signatures keep bare ids (claude, codex, antigravity). A signature from register-signature replaces an earlier one with the same id from the same plugin. A signature id that the manifest already contributes returns conflict.

Settings can also supply signatures as plain JSON. They go through the same validation, and an error names the field path, for example process_names[2]: empty name.

Contributions

{
  "id": "example.agent-tools",
  "signatures": [{
    "id": "example-agent",
    "process_names": ["example-agent"],
    "aliases": ["ea"],
    "icon": "robot",
    "actions": [{ "id": "compact", "keys": "/compact\r", "allowed_when": ["idle", "done"] }],
    "resume": ["example-agent", "--resume", "{session}"],
    "session_scope": "agent-sessions:claude"
  }],
  "commands": [{ "id": "compact", "title": "Compact agent context" }],
  "toolbar_buttons": [{
    "id": "compact", "icon": "compress", "label": "Compact",
    "command": "example.agent-tools/compact",
    "applies_to": ["example-agent"], "requires_action": "compact"
  }],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["agent.read", "agent.control", "agent.signatures"] }
}

A toolbar button has applies_to, either "all" or a list of signature ids. Use the local id for the plugin's own signatures and the bare id for built-in ones. requires_action shows the button only on panes whose signature declares that action. The button's command is a global command id.

Detector rules

  • identify runs on every detection tick for each pane that has no signature. It returns the local signature id, and the kernel adds the plugin prefix. An id the plugin did not register is ignored, the pane stays unidentified, and the kernel logs a warning.
  • classify runs for an identified pane whenever its screen revision changes.
  • Each call has a 20 ms deadline. A missed deadline keeps the previous classification, emits nothing and logs a warning.
  • A trap counts as a failure and follows the restart and disable rule: restart after 1 s, then 5 s, and disable on the third failure within 10 minutes.
  • Without the detector export a pane is identified by process_names and aliases alone. Its activity stays none, but resume, actions and submit_keys still apply.

Example 1: classifier and compact button (Rust)

This server plugin identifies example-agent, classifies its screen, and enables the Compact button only while the agent is idle. When the user presses the button, the plugin submits the compact action, which the kernel sends as /compact followed by Enter. The manifest above is the matching manifest.

use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{Classification, DetectorProcess, DetectorScreen};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::{AgentActivityEvent, CommandInvokedEvent};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::AgentActionSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

const SIGNATURE: &str = "example-agent";
const COMPACT_COMMAND: &str = "example.agent-tools/compact";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["detector"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct AgentTools;

impl Detector for AgentTools {
    fn identify(&mut self, processes: Vec<DetectorProcess>) -> Option<String> {
        let found = processes.iter().any(|process| process.name == "example-agent");
        found.then(|| SIGNATURE.to_string())
    }

    fn classify(&mut self, _signature: String, screen: DetectorScreen) -> Classification {
        let shows = |text: &str| screen.rows.iter().any(|row| row.contains(text));
        let activity = if shows("Do you want to proceed?") {
            AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval
        } else if shows("esc to interrupt") {
            AgentActivity::Working
        } else {
            AgentActivity::Idle
        };
        Classification { activity, objective: None, goal: None }
    }
}

impl Handler for AgentTools {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { node, current, .. }) => {
                    let enabled = current == AgentActivity::Idle;
                    // A pane that closed meanwhile returns not-found; nothing else depends on it.
                    let _ = agent::set_toolbar_state("compact", Some(node), enabled, None);
                }
                Event::CommandInvoked(CommandInvokedEvent { command, context, .. })
                    if command == COMPACT_COMMAND =>
                {
                    let Some(pane) = context.pane else { continue };
                    let spec = AgentActionSpec { pane, action_id: "compact".into() };
                    let key = format!("compact:{pane}");
                    submissions.push(Submission::keyed(Intent::AgentAction(spec), key));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}

Grants: agent.read for the activity event, agent.control for the toolbar state and the action, and agent.signatures for the manifest signature and the detector export.

Outcome: on a permission prompt the pane shows awaiting-approval and Compact is disabled. A press sends compact once; a second press with the same key within 10 minutes completes as duplicate.

Example 2: runtime signature and session (TypeScript)

This server plugin registers a second agent, example-agent-beta, when it activates. A command reads the session reference and the last prompt of the focused pane and writes them to the plugin log.

import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { lastPrompt, registerSignature, session } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent';

const SHOW_SESSION_COMMAND = 'example.beta-agent/show-session';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {
    // Throws PluginError (invalid-argument) when validation fails; activation then fails.
    registerSignature({
      id: 'example-agent-beta',
      processNames: ['example-agent-beta'],
      aliases: [],
      icon: 'robot',
      resume: ['example-agent-beta', '--resume', '{session}'],
      actions: [],
      sessionScope: 'agent-sessions:codex',
      submitKeys: undefined,
    });
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command !== SHOW_SESSION_COMMAND) continue;
      const pane = event.val.context.pane;
      if (pane === undefined) continue;
      const reference = session(pane);
      const prompt = lastPrompt(pane);
      log('info', `session ${reference?.path ?? 'none'}; last prompt ${prompt ?? 'none'}`);
    }
    return [];
  },
});

Grants: agent.signatures, agent.read and agent.read-prompts. The manifest also needs a commands entry with id show-session. Reading the transcript behind reference.path would also need fs.read:agent-sessions:codex, which this example does not use.

Intent and events

agent-action is an intent, Intent::AgentAction(AgentActionSpec { pane, action_id }) in Rust and { tag: 'agent-action', val: { pane, actionId } } in TypeScript. Its submission must carry a dedup-key. The kernel checks the steps below in order. A refused submission does not reserve its key, so a retry with the same key after fixing the cause is valid.

Step Outcome when it fails
Well formed, key present refused(invalid-argument); the whole batch is refused
Grant agent.control refused(not-permitted)
Key reserved already duplicate(original)
Pane exists and is an agent pane refused(not-found)
Pane restored and process started refused(pane-not-ready)
Action id in the signature refused(unsupported)
Activity allowed by allowed_when refused(conflict) with a message named after the current activity, for example agent is working
Rate: 20 per second per pane per plugin refused(rate-limited) with retry-after-ms
Write failed(code); the key stays reserved, so a retry needs a new key

Events:

Event Payload Grant Delivery
agent-identified node, signature agent.read Never dropped. Always before the first activity event of the pane.
agent-activity-changed node, previous, current, revision agent.read Never dropped.
agent-goal-changed node, goal agent.read Coalesced per node.
input-submitted node, text, source, epoch agent.read-prompts Never dropped. Without the grant, nothing derived from the text is sent.

source is one of user, plugin, scheduled or voice. epoch is the prompt counter of the pane, and it increases with each submitted prompt.

Errors and edge cases

  • register-signature returns invalid-argument for a rule that breaks the signature limits (id, process names, aliases, icon, action count or key size). The message names the field path. It returns conflict for an id the manifest already contributes.
  • Two signatures from different origins that match one process name do not fail. The user's signature wins over a plugin signature, which wins over a built-in one, and the overlap is logged as a warning.
  • set-toolbar-state returns not-found for a button that is not the plugin's own or a pane that does not exist, and not-permitted when the grant is missing. Its state lasts until the plugin changes it. A plugin restart resets each button to its manifest state, and a revoked grant withdraws the state.
  • agents() returns an empty list when agent.read is declined. view, session and last_prompt return none, because these functions have no error channel.
  • A grant revoked at run time takes effect on the next call.
  • A pane has no activity before its agent-identified event. Restored panes return none for last_prompt until a new prompt is submitted, because the text is not in the snapshot.

What the user sees

The toolbar of an agent pane shows each button that matches applies_to and requires_action. A disabled button is greyed out and does not respond. The tree shows each identified pane's activity through node-view.agent.

Transcript, model and signals

model, prompt-epoch, the typed transcript and the events signal-changed and agent-model-changed are described in Agent transcript and signals. They need agent.read, and agent.transcript (high risk) for the transcript. user-line-submitted is described in Terminal reads.

Requirement ids for this page: [PRI-010], [PRI-011], [PRI-012], [PRI-013], [PRI-015]. See the requirements index.
